title: JetBrains Surveyed Nearly 30,000 Developers: 96% Already Use AI Tools, but 46% Report a Diminished Sense of Ownership Over Code

content_html:
AI writing code is no longer just a novelty for a few people; it is the default setup across the entire industry—and the costs have surfaced along with it. On November 27, JetBrains released its "State of the Developer Ecosystem 2026" report: this annual survey, now in its tenth year, gathered feedback from 28,945 developers worldwide. 96% of employed developers use at least one AI tool in their work, but 46% feel less "ownership" over the code, while 55% believe their creativity has improved.

Agents Take Over 60% of Tasks

The tool landscape is layered: Claude Code leads with 39% usage, followed by GitHub Copilot at 21%, ChatGPT at 17%, and OpenAI Codex and Claude at 16% each. The deeper penetration is at the agent level—more than half of developers who use coding agents say that over the past month, more than 60% of development tasks were completed by AI agents; the more experienced people are, the better they understand how to feed agents project context, rules files, and verification methods. The efficiency math is also easy: 76% say coding is faster, 73% say overall efficiency has improved, and 48% say mental effort has decreased.

The Saved Time Is Paid Back

Behind the benefits is another ledger: 58% of developers spend more time reviewing AI-generated code, 42% spend more time correcting or rewriting it, and 38% struggle to get AI to produce the expected results. Views diverge by experience: among those with 1 to 2 years of experience, 60% think AI solutions are better than what they would write themselves, while among those with 16+ years of experience, only 47% think so. Organizational adoption is also layered: in 54% of small organizations, more than 80% of colleagues use AI, compared with only 37% of large organizations. When 60% of tasks are handed over to agents, is code still "my work"? That 46% sense of loss is the answer.
